> Run modules in order (00, 01, 02, 03, 05, 06); each assumes the previous ones have run (objects/functions in the environment) or loads the provided derived data from `data/` via module 00.

2. SIMULATIONS
  now i have all the components of the thrust power equation tied to empirical data 
  and can predict the mass of a calf based on its age and maternal length (van Aswegen et al., age-specific growth costs)
  and the mass of a mother based on its length (van Aswegen et al., age-specific growth costs) to get BMR
  and I know the number of fluke strokes per minute during rest dives and other behavior for mothers and calves

  2b. simulate Metabolic thrust cost (J/s) using the thrust power and monte carlo simulations around literature values for       metabolic efficiency and propulsive efficiency

```{r}
YatesUProp <- read.csv(file.path(rds_dir, "yates_uprop.csv"))
colnames(YatesUProp) <- c("Feathering", "a", "b", "c", "d", "Equation")
YatesUProp <- YatesUProp %>% mutate(across(c(Feathering, a, b, c, d), as.numeric))



# u_prop: derived empirically from Yates (1983) lookup tables
# values consistent with Potvin et al. 2021 (0.7-0.8)
# already computed in calc_u_prop_vectorized - no change needed

# u_met: fixed at 0.25 following Potvin et al. 2021
# "4 Joules of muscle chemical energy to generate 1 Joule of mechanical work"
# sensitivity analysis across 0.1-0.4 (Gough et al. 2025) reported in supplement



```


  2d. simulate mother and calf pairs of varying realistic lengths, masses, and ages using the van Aswegen et al. growth models (age-specific growth costs) and simulate BMR 

    d1. making calf age length mass traces properly
    "uncertainty in morphometric scaling was propagated via lower and upper parameter envelopes, while primary analyses used       mean   estimates"
```{r}





ages <- 1:110
mothers <- seq(10, 15, by = 0.1)

grid <- expand.grid(
  Age = ages,
  ML = mothers
)

#for just mean!! could use 95 and 5% CI's later 
calf_mass_table <- grid %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # relative length (mean only)
    Calf_RL = 0.737106 - (0.737106 - 0.3504304) * exp(-0.006740519 * Age),
    
    # total length
    Calf_TL = Calf_RL * ML,
    
    # body volume
    BV = exp(-3.991 + 2.881 * log(Calf_TL)),
    
    # tissue masses (mean only)
    Musc_Mass = BV * (exp(1.934 + 0.657 * log(Calf_TL)) / 100) * 972.6259,
    Bone_Mass = BV * (exp(4.441 - 0.705 * log(Calf_TL)) / 100) * 1123.534,
    Visc_Mass = BV * (exp(3.276 - 0.369 * log(Calf_TL)) / 100) * 953.707,
    Blood_Mass = BV * 0.06 * 1048.657,
    
    Blubber_Mass =
      (BV -
         Musc_Mass / 972.6259 -
         Bone_Mass / 1123.534 -
         Visc_Mass / 953.707 -
         Blood_Mass / 1048.657
      ) * 986,
    
    # total mass (kg)
    Mass_kg =
      Musc_Mass +
      Bone_Mass +
      Visc_Mass +
      Blubber_Mass +
      Blood_Mass
  )

# full version - keep all tissue columns for growth cost calculation
calf_mass_table_full <- calf_mass_table  # save before selecting

calf_mass_table <- calf_mass_table %>%
  dplyr::select(Age, Calf_TL, ML, Mass_kg)
```
  
  
    d2. make mother masses based on length from the van Aswegen et al. body-mass model (age-specific growth costs)
```{r}

mothers <- seq(10, 15, by = 0.1)

mother_table <- data.frame(
  MotherLength = mothers
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    MotherMass_kg = predict_mother_mass(MotherLength)
  )

```

  2e. simulate these mothers and calves in different proportions of behaviors to get variations of daily energy expenditure 
  The key methodological point is that within each of the n=500 iterations, locomotion, BMR, and HIF are all sampled simultaneously from their respective uncertainty distributions and then summed - so the output CI reflects their joint uncertainty correctly. Growth costs are the one component added as summarized values post-hoc, which is honest to state explicitly: their uncertainty is propagated separately from the van Aswegen et al. published growth models (age-specific growth costs) and combined additively at the summary level. 
  
big simulation of BMR, HIF and movement costs
```{r}

# check where area goes negative on average
test_lengths <- seq(min(full_table$Calf_TL), max(full_table$Calf_TL), by = 0.1)

mean_area <- sapply(test_lengths, function(bl) {
  mean(predict_area(bl, n = 200))
})

min_safe_length <- min(test_lengths[mean_area > 0])
cat("Minimum safe calf length:", min_safe_length, "\n")

# then filter
full_table <- full_table %>%
  filter(Calf_TL >= min_safe_length)

behavior_grid <- seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.1)

p_rest <- behavior_grid
p_active <- 1 - p_rest

```

actually run simulation
```{r}
results <- list()

library(furrr)
library(future)

plan(multisession, workers = parallel::detectCores() - 3)

results <- future_map_dfr(behavior_grid, function(p) {
  
  purrr::map_dfr(1:nrow(full_table), function(i) {
    simulate_daily_energy(
      full_table[i, ],
      p_rest          = p,
      n               = 200,
      yatesCT         = YatesCT,
      yatesUProp      = YatesUProp,
      calf_propstroke = calf_propstroke,
      mom_propstroke  = mom_propstroke
    )
  })
  
}, .options = furrr_options(
  seed = TRUE,
  globals = c(
    "full_table", "YatesCT", "YatesUProp",
    "calf_propstroke", "mom_propstroke",
    "simulate_daily_energy",
    "predict_chord", "predict_area", "predict_frequency",
    "predict_speed", "predict_speed_calf", "predict_speed_mom",   # <- add these
    "predict_stroke_rate", "predict_stroke_calf", "predict_stroke_mom",  # <- and these if used
    "predict_prop_fluking", "predict_prop_fluking_calf",
    "calc_metabolic_power_full", "calc_thrust_power_full",
    "calc_Ct_vectorized", "calc_u_prop_vectorized",
    "get_ct_coeffs", "get_uprop_coeffs",
    "draw_coefs", "draw_lmer_coefs", "get_resid_sigma",
    "fixed_effects_table", "vcov_list", "models", "model_sigmas"
  )
))


```

model checks
```{r}
# test on a single row to check CI stability across n
test_row <- full_table[50, ]

ns <- c(50, 100, 200, 500, 1000)

convergence_check <- purrr::map_dfr(ns, function(n) {
  res <- simulate_daily_energy(
    test_row, p_rest = 0.5, n = n,
    yatesCT = YatesCT, yatesUProp = YatesUProp,
    calf_propstroke = calf_propstroke,
    mom_propstroke  = mom_propstroke
  )
  res$n <- n
  res
})

convergence_check %>%
  dplyr::select(n, calf_total_mean, calf_total_lwr, calf_total_upr,
                  mom_total_mean,  mom_total_lwr,  mom_total_upr)

# run one row and inspect components separately
test <- simulate_daily_energy(
  full_table[50, ], p_rest = 0.5, n = 200,
  yatesCT = YatesCT, yatesUProp = YatesUProp,
  calf_propstroke = calf_propstroke,
  mom_propstroke  = mom_propstroke
)

# look at components separately
test %>% dplyr::select(
  mom_BMR_mean, mom_loco_mean, mom_total_mean,
  calf_BMR_mean, calf_HIF_mean, calf_loco_mean, calf_total_mean
)

U     <- 1.5    # m/s
f     <- 0.21   # Hz - more realistic for large humpback
BL    <- 11     # m
chord <- 0.9    # m - check against your chord model prediction
area  <- 2.5    # m2 - check against your area model prediction

# first verify what your empirical models actually predict for an 11m whale
cat("predicted chord:", mean(predict_chord(11, n = 200)), "\n")
cat("predicted area:",  mean(predict_area(11,  n = 200)), "\n")
cat("predicted freq:",  mean(predict_frequency(11, n = 200)), "\n")

# then run the power chain with realistic inputs
h <- 0.1 * BL

PT <- calc_thrust_power_full(
  U = rep(U, 100), f = rep(f, 100),
  body_length = BL, chord = rep(chord, 100),
  area = rep(area, 100), yatesCT = YatesCT
)
cat("PT mean (W):", mean(PT), "\n")

u_prop <- calc_u_prop_vectorized(
  U = rep(U, 100), f = rep(f, 100),
  body_length = BL, chord = rep(chord, 100),
  yatesUProp = YatesUProp
)
cat("u_prop mean:", mean(u_prop), "\n")

Pmet <- PT / (0.25 * u_prop)
cat("Pmet mean (W):", mean(Pmet), "\n")
cat("Pmet per hour (MJ):", mean(Pmet) * 3600 / 1e6, "\n")
cat("Pmet per day (MJ):", mean(Pmet) * 86400 / 1e6, "\n")

cat("prop fluke rest mom:",  mean(predict_prop_fluking(mom_propstroke, "rest",  200)), "\n")
cat("prop fluke other mom:", mean(predict_prop_fluking(mom_propstroke, "other", 200)), "\n")
```
